outcome: Maternal outcomes (disease course severity, organ dysfunction, disseminated intravascular coagulation, maternal mortality, preeclampsia, need for surgical intervention, improvement in general health condition post-delivery)
Neonatal outcomes (preterm births, miscarriage, NICU admissions, perinatal mortality, intrauterine fetal demise)
cohort: 32 pregnant women diagnosed with acute pancreatitis during pregnancy or the postpartum period who were treated at Aga Khan University Hospital in Karachi, Pakistan, between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2021.
finding: The study found that gallstones were the most common etiology of acute pancreatitis in pregnancy (APIP), and APIP was associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia and preterm births.
mod_finding: 13 (40.6%) patients underwent an emergency cesarean section.
